---
title: "Glossary"
description: "One-line definitions of the terms this specification uses."
---

## The notation

| Term | Definition |
|:--|:--|
| **Studyflow** | A coordination notation for experimental research: one representation of a study's process that is machine-readable, human-understandable, and executable. |
| **a studyflow** | One study written in that notation: one object, one file. |
| **BPMN** | Business Process Model and Notation, ISO/IEC 19510. Studyflow is a domain-specific profile of it, so a studyflow opens in generic BPMN tools. |
| **Element set** | A schema declaring types, attributes, and presets. Four load always; three load on request. See [Extending the notation](../concepts/extending.qmd). |
| **Coordination model** | The half of a program that binds activities into an ensemble — ordering, dependencies, and what each stage hands the next — as opposed to the computation each activity performs. |

## The object

| Term | Definition |
|:--|:--|
| **Node** | Any element of the graph: an event, an activity, a gateway, or a data element. |
| **Edge** | A typed connection between two nodes: sequence flow, data association, or message flow. |
| **Control-flow graph** | The sub-graph of sequence-flow edges — what happens next. |
| **Data-flow graph** | The sub-graph of data-association edges — what each step reads and writes. |
| **Activity** | A step: a task, a sub-process, or a call to another studyflow. Drawn as a rounded rectangle. |
| **Event** | A point where something happens rather than is done: entry, a timer firing, an exit. Drawn as a circle. |
| **Gateway** | A point where the path splits or rejoins. Drawn as a diamond. |
| **Boundary event** | A circle sitting on an activity's own border: a second way out of that step, with its own outgoing edge. |
| **Sub-process** | An activity containing a whole flow. Expanding or collapsing one changes the drawing, never what runs. |
| **Pool** | A whole party in a study — a participant group, a model, an instrument — drawn as a band around its own flow. |
| **Choreography** | A drawing of the exchanges between two parties rather than of one party's own path. |
| **Property** | Run state a condition reads by name, declared by a container and never drawn. |
| **Scope** | The container that declares a value and fixes how long it lives. |
| **Well-formed** | Satisfying the conditions in [The studyflow object](../concepts/object.qmd#well-formedness). |

## Views and runs

| Term | Definition |
|:--|:--|
| **Projection** | A view: the subset of the object selected by a predicate, carrying its attributes unchanged. A projection discards and never adds. |
| **Study view** | The diagram itself — the projection that keeps everything. |
| **Timeline view** | The projection over elements carrying `onset`, `duration`, or `progress`. |
| **Checklist view** | The projection over elements carrying reporting items. |
| **Provenance view** | The projection over the record entries. |
| **Run** | One traversal of the control-flow graph: one participant's session, or one pass of a pipeline. |
| **Seed** | The root of the pseudo-random state. Pinned, every gateway draw replays; unset, a run draws one and records it. |
| **Checkpoint** | A step finishing, a gateway deciding, or a run opening or closing. |
| **Prospective provenance** | The plan: what should happen. A studyflow at deposit. |
| **Retrospective provenance** | The record: what did happen. Accumulated in the same file as the plan. |
| **Deviation** | The difference between the two, obtained as a diff rather than by comparing documents. |

## The tools

| Term | Definition |
|:--|:--|
| **The modeler** | The browser application where a studyflow is drawn and edited. |
| **The browser runner** | The executor that administers a studyflow to one participant, screen by screen. |
| **The Python runner** | The executor that runs the data-facing half of a studyflow, calling the software each step names. |
| **The command line** | The `studyflow` binary: convert, validate, inspect, and dispatch a run. |
